items.title: Port Credit's 130-Year-Old United Church Could Become City-Owned Event Venue
items.summary: According to insauga.com, the City of Mississauga is in the process of buying a more than 130-year-old United Church property at 151 Lakeshore Rd. W. in Port Credit, which has been listed for sale for nearly six months. Then-Mayor Carolyn Parrish announced in July that the city planned to turn the building into an event venue and a permanent home for the Canada Virtuoso Ensemble. The church, most recently known as Christ First United Church, amalgamated with the Clarkson Christ First United Church on Mazo Crescent in 2019 and moved its regular services there the same year. A Spanish-language congregation currently holds services in the Port Credit building on typical Sundays, according to a church spokesperson. The congregation is also planning a Candlelight Service at the Port Credit church in December, the spokesperson said.

items.title: Credit Valley Conservation Warns of Unsafe Water Levels Ahead of Weekend Rain
items.summary: According to Credit Valley Conservation, residents in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon should stay away from rivers and streams over the next few days as widespread rainfall moves into the region. The conservation authority issued a water safety statement Thursday warning that an approaching low-pressure system could bring over 30 millimetres of rain by Saturday, with a chance of freezing rain in the Upper Credit watershed. CVC said the watershed received no rain in the past 10 days, so soil is dry and flooding of the Credit River and its major tributaries is not expected. Even so, officials warned some watersheds could see higher flows, making areas near culverts, bridges and dams unsafe for anglers, canoeists, hikers and pets. The statement stays in effect through Sunday, and the authority said it will keep monitoring conditions and issue updates as needed.

items.title: Peel Inspectors Shut Down a Dundas Street Restaurant and Bakery
items.summary: According to Peel Public Health, inspectors temporarily closed a Mississauga restaurant and bakery during a routine food safety inspection. Revrea's Grill & Bakeshop, located at 1057 Dundas St., was ordered to close when it was inspected on Nov. 25, the health unit says. Peel Public Health routinely checks local restaurants, cocktail bars, bakeries and takeout establishments to ensure compliance with the Health Protection and Promotion Act. A green pass indicates a business is meeting food safety and operational standards, according to the region of Peel. The health unit did not specify in its public summary what led inspectors to order the closure.

items.title: Peel Police Say 'Project Twilight' Suspect Faces Dozens of Charges in Five Luxury Car Home Invasions
items.summary: According to Peel police, a man already in custody has been charged with dozens of offences connected to five home invasions in Toronto, Mississauga and Brampton between May 29 and June 2. Investigators believe the break-ins were carried out by the same group of three or four suspects, who forcibly entered residences in the early morning hours and demanded vehicle keys from occupants. Several luxury vehicles, including BMW and Mercedes models, were stolen or targeted in the attacks, though no victims were physically injured, police said. Toronto and Peel police coordinated on a probe dubbed Project Twilight and arrested the man along with a 20-year-old woman from Hamilton on June 8. Det. Cst. Nathan Ball told a news conference Thursday that investigators no longer believe the woman was involved, and said the investigation remains ongoing with more arrests expected.

items.title: Peel Police Set to Detail New Home Invasion Probe Tied to Luxury Vehicle Thefts
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Peel police are set to release details of a new probe into home invasions across the GTA targeting luxury vehicles. Investigators say auto theft has dropped in Mississauga and Brampton in recent years, but it remains a top concern, especially when a home break-in is involved, since that puts residents at risk. The announcement follows a separate bust less than two weeks ago in which a dozen men face 231 combined charges over stolen luxury SUVs and other high-value vehicles taken from driveways across the GTA. Police say that ring moved the stolen vehicles out of Ontario within days, loading them into containers bound overseas from the Port of Montreal. The probe, led by Peel's commercial auto crime squad with the Canada Border Services Agency, turned up a broader criminal network across the region, investigators said.

items.title: Mississauga Councillor Says Malton Greenway Sees Eight Encampment Removals a Month
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga council voted unanimously on Nov. 25 to study improvements for the Malton Greenway after Ward 5 Coun. Natalie Hart said years of neglect and encampments have left residents afraid to use the trail. Hart told council and city staff that the two-kilometre park and trail in the city's north end is meant to connect people but currently cannot be used safely. She said the area has seen more encampments than resident activity over the past couple of years, with crews now removing roughly eight encampments a month. Hart's motion directs city staff to explore options for cleaning up and improving safety along the greenway. The councillor pointed to an incident the same morning in which a parks crew was called to clear garbage illegally dumped behind a nearby mall.
